full_judgment: 81. As to the submission of Mr Md Hatem Ali that when the confession becomes doubtful, the conviction and sentence based solely on such confession cannot be sustainable in law, there is no dispute about this proposition of law as enunciated in the case of Masum Howlader vs State reported in 2 BLC 173. But in the present case, it has been found that all the confessions are true and voluntary and free from allurement, inducement, coercion and intimidation and that those have been corroborated by the medical and circumstantial evidence on record. Viewed from this stand-point, the confession of any of the condemned-appellants is not doubtful. Accordingly, the question of reversal of the impugned order of conviction and sentence is out of the question. So the reliance of Mr Md Hatem Ali on the decision reported in 1 MLR 164 does not help him in any manner.
